name: Alpex Solar Limited
sector: Solar modules, cell manufacturing expansion and EPC
identity_note: Legal name and security checked in cited issuer/exchange filing.
summary: Alpex is a rapidly scaled solar manufacturer entering a much more capital-intensive cell business. Historical growth is real, but weak cash conversion, large funding requirements and deficient financial controls prevent a quality-compounder conclusion. The apparent low trailing P/E does not price a fully funded, fully qualified cell operation. Conditional base return is about 17.05%, only marginally above the 15% hurdle, and sensitive to completion costs, cash conversion and technology renewal. Classification: cyclical expansion watchlist, not an unconditional purchase.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Alpex Solar Limited, NSE SME ALPEXSOLAR, ISIN INE0R4701017. Cutoff 20 October 2026; observed 19 October close ₹763.30, lot 100. March 2026 issued shares 25, 543, 000; 1, 077, 000 potential warrant shares are included conservatively without unreceived exercise money. Reports use consolidated Ind AS; FY24 profit is the later Ind AS comparative, not the older GAAP figure. Historical evidence confidence is Medium: primary audited aggregate accounts and reviewed Q1 support material model inputs, but an expressly qualified internal-control report and incomplete project allocation limit certainty. Forecast uncertainty is separately high. No live price, approval, cash balance or credit availability is inferred.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.10; Growth Quality GQS 5.00; IAS 5.625. Canonical factors: GOV 4; MOAT 5; REV 8; DUR 6; CAP 6; CASH 3; BAL 4; EXEC 5; EARN 6; R 7; D 3; P 5; L 8. All factors use canonical weights without reweighting. Persistent CASH 3 caps GQS at 5; it is not a misconduct verdict. R 7 is narrowly earned at 17.0466% exact IRR, not rounded 17%. Higher financing fees/rates or full project renewal reduce R to 6; completion 750 cr or WC 32% reduce R to 5. These scenarios lower IAS by 0.35 or 0.70 without turning a watchlist into a proven compounder.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Founded in 1993, Alpex manufactures solar modules and related systems, supplies solar-pump/EPC solutions and has expanded into aluminium frames and cells. FY26 product sales ₹2214.1912 cr dominate services ₹5.1083 cr and other operating income. Group revenue ₹2223.2719 cr is close to parent ₹2218.1636 cr, so the core manufacturing parent dominates. Management reported 2.4 GW module capacity moving toward 3.6 GW, 12, 000 MT frames and a 2.2 GW G12R TOPCon cell project. Nameplate is not qualified saleable output. Cells consumed in its own modules are not counted again as external revenue. No unfunded wafer/glass or IPP ambitions enter base earnings.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Module qualification, OEM relationships, execution scale and frame integration help, but commodity input/output spreads and technological competition limit pricing durability. Official September 16 ALMM-I includes an Alpex Tower 2 module entry 799 MW and a separate revised Surajpur entry 956 MW; these are unit/model-specific approvals, not proof of cell approval or total output. The latest retrieved official ALMM-II compilation is October 8; its 31 pages, including OCR of scanned pages, contain no Alpex entry located in this review. This is a dated list observation, not an allegation of illegal operation or proof that no later approval exists. The July application and September inauguration do not substitute for model-level qualification. Modules can use approved third-party cells where required.

Peer Websol’s August primary presentation reports Q1 FY27 revenue ₹373 cr and EBITDA excluding other income ₹126 cr, 33.7% margin, versus 47.3% a year earlier. Its announced ₹270 cr 600-to 750 MW TOPCon upgrade shows both strong current cell economics and substantial refresh investment. It is not a like-for-like Alpex margin or P/E benchmark: Websol already has operating cell production, different technology/mix and balance-sheet scale. No market peer multiple is copied.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Consolidated FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 operating revenue was ₹194.6801/412.5998/780.1512/2223.2719 cr. Three-year CAGR is 125.19%; annual additions ₹217.9197/367.5514/1443.1207 cr. Four comparable revenue observations support strong growth, but not a claimed five-year organic CAGR. FY24 Ind AS profit ₹29.0887 cr differs from older GAAP ₹26.5596 cr; the later consistent comparative is used. FY26 group PAT ₹201.513 cr versus ₹83.4779 cr rose sharply; owner PAT ₹201.4726 cr excludes small minority earnings.

Reviewed Q1 FY27 revenue ₹503.4246 cr versus ₹380.3219 cr rose 32.37%, but PAT ₹39.867 cr versus ₹42.2932 cr fell 5.74%. Core EBITDA excluding other income is approximately ₹74.535 cr, 14.81% of sales; the presentation’s ₹78.43 cr EBITDA is not treated as identical core operating profit. Faster volume and higher nominal sales need not translate into durable owner earnings.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Domestic solar demand is large, but policy is not an unlimited margin guarantee. MNRE’s July 18 memorandum gives only net-metering/open-access projects commissioned through 31 December 2026 a limited cell-list exemption; it explicitly rejects a blanket extension. List-I module obligations remain distinct. Competition and cell/module price convergence can compress scarcity margins.

The August call described roughly ₹890 cr cell-project spending/budget, approximately ₹341 cr debt for that project, five-year depreciation and possible seven-year operation. Project debt is not total group debt. July’s fire filing described a limited utility-area event and resumed normal operations; August management acknowledged about one month of cell-start delay. September 17 records inauguration, not verified commercial output, yield or collections. Base FY27 revenue ₹2800 cr, rising to ₹5250 cr terminal, assumes a paid, qualified ramp. Base margin peaks 22% then normalizes 15%, rather than perpetuating management’s 35–40% cell-only margin ambition.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The FY26 internal-control opinion is expressly qualified: IT general/application controls have a material weakness. The financial-statement opinion is unmodified, and the auditor says the weakness was considered in audit procedures and did not change that financial opinion. These are different conclusions; neither a blanket clean-governance claim nor automatic proof of misstated accounts is justified. Database-level audit trails were not enabled throughout the year. Management says SAP and controls are being strengthened; independent remediation remains unverified.

Prior audit-committee approval was absent for ₹6.3264 cr promoter-group managerial remuneration and several related transactions; quarterly omnibus reviews were also missed. The annual report records June 4 ratification. Transactions listed include ₹27.6416 cr subsidiary dealings, ₹4.6614 cr step-down novation/reimbursement, ₹1.2754 cr associate generator purchase, ₹8.4799 cr other connected dealings and ₹33.137 cr JV sales. Ratification remedies the approval record but does not independently establish arm’s-length value or collection.

June’s secretarial-auditor resignation states professional commitments; it is not a statutory-auditor resignation. The ₹7080 late-filing fine was paid and is economically minor; threatened freezing in a notice is not evidence of an executed freeze. The presentation’s near-debt-free caption is not reconciled to ₹506.67 cr audited drawn debt and is not relied upon. No fraud finding is inferred.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY24/FY25/FY26 CFO was −₹8.0157/+₹68.8368/−₹115.6122 cr. Total −₹54.7911 cr versus ₹314.0796 cr PAT gives −17.44% conversion. FY25’s positive conversion is important contrary evidence; two weak years and the current funding gap support CASH 3, not a claim that growth inventory is misconduct. FY26 operating cash absorbed ₹256.4608 crinventory, ₹130.9803 crreceivables and ₹76.4014 crother current assets, partly funded by ₹92.0451 crpayables. Cash PPE ₹241.1973 cr, intangibles ₹4.7582 cr and capital advances ₹85.7437 cr total ₹331.6992 cr; CFO less this spending is −₹447.3114 cr.

Group debt rose ₹72.0791 cr to ₹506.6709 cr, excluding ₹29.846 crleases. Current/noncurrent restricted deposits total ₹131.2492 cr and are not free net cash. Related receivables include ₹25.0127 cr Alpex NVNRConsortium; its negative investment balance and 70% constructive project obligation deserve attention. No unsupported guarantee loss is added to base. Disputed income-tax ₹1.0903 cr is contingent; net current tax ₹45.488 cr is a separate existing liability, settled once. Bank guarantees ₹82.5806 cr are not automatically drawn debt.

The preferential issue is arithmetically reconciled:1, 069, 600 shares×₹1212=₹129.63552 crgross, less ₹18.4783 crshare-issue expenses≈₹111.1573 crnet financing cash. The unusually high 14.25% cost lacks a verified beneficiary breakdown here, but is not a missing-cash contradiction. Monitoring shows ₹162.27 crreceived/utilized including 25%warrant deposits; ₹97.8993 cr remains unpaid. The June corrigendum changes headings/comparative-year labeling, not disclosed amounts.

Core operating EBIT ₹295.6983 cr excludes other income and exceptional loss. At 25% normalized tax, NOPAT ₹221.7737 cr on average equity+drawn debt+lease capital≈₹696.77 cr gives 31.83%; incremental NOPAT ₹134.182 cr on≈₹803.08 cr new capital gives 16.71%. The latter is a one-year proxy, not an achieved cell-project IRR. The issue-cost denominator matters: ₹18.4783 cr equals 14.25% of the equity tranche but about 7.10% of the combined ₹260.17 cr equity-plus-warrant commitment. The report does not separately allocate those costs by tranche, so 14.25% is not asserted as a verified standalone equity placement commission.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Entry ₹763.30 implies about ₹1949.69 cr equity value on current shares, 9.68 times FY26 owner PAT; including all potential warrants without unpaid cash gives 10.09 times. Trailing earnings are not the cash cost of completing the next phase.

Base/bear/bull terminal prices are ₹1676.83/₹45.86/₹5623.82, five-year IRRs 17.05%/−43.02%/+49.10%. Base 15%hurdle entry is ₹833.68. Annual FY27–FY31 schedules plus a FY32 stub end 19 October 2031. Opening Marchcash is dated, not claimed as current; the full FY27 forecast bridges unreported interim cash movements. Net tax, accrued finance costs, restricted IPOcash and an analyst ₹25 cr operating reserve are deducted once. Restricted collateral grows with sales.

Base completion cash ₹603 cr is an explicit estimate:₹890 cr project description less roughly ₹287 cr March CWIP/capital advances, whose project allocation is not fully disclosed. ₹450/750 cr sensitivities bracket this assumption; it is not presented as a signed remaining commitment. Five-year cell depreciation follows management’s stated convention, but life and renewal are separate. Base major renewal atfiveyears is 60% of project cost, with 30%/100%/deferred scenarios; reusable land/buildings prevent treating full plant replacement as mandatory. Routine module/operating maintenance is separate. No building/land renewal fact is invented.

Interest 11.5% includes half-year new borrowing with circular funding solved. Base debt ceiling ₹900 cr and 2.5 times EBITDA are analytical limits, not sanctioned facilities. Cash deficits require ₹177.83 cr hypothetical gross equity at 30% below entry plus 5% fees, increasing shares to 2.99481 cr; cumulative new borrowing ₹393.33 cr is also required. Warrants at ₹1212 are out of the money and their unpaid ₹97.8993 cr is excluded. Terminal 12 times normalized operating NOPAT is an analyst cyclical assumption, not an observed peer multiple. Full renewal lowers IRR 15.33%; ₹750 cr completion 13.46%; 32% WC 13.40%; 12% terminal margin 8.67%. These materially alter return attractiveness.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Bear starts ₹2300 cr sales, later reaches ₹3400 cr, uses 12% terminal margin, 32% working capital and higher completion cost. It requires ₹775.10 cr gross equity and ₹752.73 cr cumulative new debt even under the model; conditional terminal ₹45.86 loses about 94% of entry value. Severe funding needs are larger and modeled equity is exhausted. If investors/lenders do not provide these hypothetical funds, operational distress may occur earlier than the model.

Delayed qualification, low cell yield, declining module prices, GST/receivable delays, expensive NCD/refinancing and simultaneous new technology investment can reinforce each other. Credit stresses ₹25/50 cr reduce opening recoverable working capital, charge noncash PAT and add the impairment back in CFO; replacement funding enters once through the closing WC requirement. They are not expected losses, immediate second cash payments or asserted misconduct. Minority/associate assets receive no separate optimistic recovery value.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five/ten times ₹763.30 requires ₹3816.50/₹7633 per share. At 20 times attributable PAT and 2.662 cr initial potential shares, required owner profit is about ₹507.97/₹1015.95 cr, versus FY26 ₹201.4726 cr. At 10% net margin, revenue would need ₹5079.7/₹10159.5 cr before additional equity dilution. Base funding raises the share count further. Bull exceeds 5 times only with a much faster qualified ramp, 20% terminal margin, low cash-cycle demands and 16 times operating NOPAT, plus funded technology renewal. Capacity announcements alone do not establish that joint outcome.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track model-level ALMM-II enlistment and verified saleable cell output/yield, not inauguration; actual cell/module external sales and internal consumption; residual capex paid versus advances and the project-specific financing bridge; cash collections, GSTassets and inventories; JVreceivables/constructive obligations; actual available funded credit versus nonfunded rating limits; warrant exercise/expiry and new equity terms; audit-committee approvals, IT-control remediation and audit trail operation; customer demand and ASP versus cell/wafer prices; technology-refresh budget. A renewed profit surge without cash, or funding unavailable within the modeled range, breaks the expansion thesis.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Cyclical, capital-intensive expansion watchlist. BQS 5.10, capped GQS 5.00, conditional IAS 5.625. The base return is only just in R 7, and plausible financing/renewal stresses lower it. A lower price improves expected return but does not cure unqualified output, weak controls or missing committed capital. No trade or position allocation is implied.

All 60 market sessions are observed. 20/60 session mean turnover ₹3.2540/4.0588 cr and medians ₹2.9753/3.1965 cr support a 0.336 day arithmetic exit for ₹5 lakh at 5% participation using the slower median. Latest 39, 300 shares, 243 trades, ₹3.0137 cr turnover; one 100-share lot ₹76, 330. L 8 discounts unobserved live spread/depth and lot granularity. October 19 REG1, effective October 21, has only the generic SME irregular-trading caution active among decoded fields. No narrow PAN/ESM/ASM/GSM restriction is invented; inactive fields are not universal regulatory clearance.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports, reviewed Q1, management calls, monitoring report, current credit letter, corporate events and official MNRE/NSE documents underpin this review. Material statements are separated from calculations and analyst assumptions. Remaining gaps are actual qualified cell output; the project-specific cost-to-complete and unrestricted funding bridge; issue-expense beneficiary breakdown; independent remediation of the qualified controls; current collections and JVobligation settlement; actual warrant exercise; live depth. Those gaps bound a conditional financed model, rather than being hidden by a simple P/E target. An adverse correction undermining audited aggregate inputs would make G 2 critical and IAS NS; lack of funding can invalidate modeled survival. Peer work is an operating comparison, not a transplanted valuation.

valuation.status: Conditional integrated manufacturing forecast, not management guidance or approved financing
assumption_basis: The opening March 2026 balance sheet is dated. The full FY27 cash bridge includes unreported pre-entry April–October movements and forward funding needs; it is not an observed October bank or debt balance.

Opening cash is ₹29.5865 crore, less ₹0.925 crore of restricted IPO money, a ₹25 crore operating reserve, ₹45.488 crore of net tax liabilities and ₹1.7204 crore of accrued interest. GST and ordinary statutory balances remain in operating working capital. Tax liabilities and guarantees are not charged twice.

Restricted deposits of ₹131.2492 crore are excluded from free cash. Additional collateral is funded explicitly, with no assumed terminal release. The current bank-balance line of ₹120.1409 crore differs from the related footnote of ₹119.9409 crore by ₹0.2 crore; neither balance is credited as freely available cash.

Management described a ₹890 crore cell-project budget. March total capital work in progress of ₹174.9261 crore plus capital advances of ₹112.2923 crore is approximately ₹287.22 crore. The base remaining spend of ₹603 crore assumes these balances relate to that project and excludes any further already-paid cell assets. This allocation is an analyst estimate, not a disclosed commitment. Remaining-spend sensitivities of ₹450 crore and ₹750 crore test that uncertainty. The annual report’s nil capital-commitment disclosure does not establish zero future investment.

Annual maintenance capex is 2.5% of sales in the base case and includes module maintenance. Cells consumed internally do not create separate group revenue. The base EBITDA margin peaks at 22% and falls to 15% at the terminal date, below management’s 35–40% cell-margin discussion because group mix, import costs, competition and normalization of scarcity pricing matter. Terminal revenue of ₹5,250 crore corresponds roughly to 2.4 GW at ₹22 per watt; this is a scale cross-check, not a mechanical forecast. Falling selling prices would require more output. No earnings from an unfunded 5 GW wafer/glass project or 100 MW independent-power project are included.

The five-year cell-depreciation assumption comes from management’s call. The ₹30 crore annual normalization for existing assets is below the ₹40 crore annualized Q1 total before cell operations. Terminal earnings retain a full replacement depreciation charge rather than benefiting from fully depreciated equipment. Major cell-technology refurbishment is funded in the final stub at 60% of project cost, approximately five years after the September 2026 start. Sensitivities cover 30%, 100% and deferred renewal. The 60% estimate reflects possible reuse of land, buildings and utilities; it is not a verified equipment-cost breakdown or mandatory full-plant replacement. Management’s five-year depreciation and expected seven-year operation are distinct from compulsory replacement at five years. Routine maintenance and major refurbishment are separate, and no future wafer/glass project is charged. Cash lease payments of ₹5.6486 crore are deducted before operating valuation, so lease debt is not also subtracted. Leases do not create free cash.

Interest is 11.5% on opening debt plus a half-year charge on new borrowing, solved iteratively. The ₹125 crore NCD carries 14.75%, compared with disclosed bank working-capital rates of 7.76–8.99%; a 14.75% financing-rate stress is included. Rated bank facilities of ₹1,078 crore include non-fund-based facilities and are not available cash. The base analytical debt ceiling of ₹900 crore and 2.5 times EBITDA is not approved credit. Remaining gaps require hypothetical equity at a 30% discount to entry price, plus issue fees. If financing is unavailable, failure may replace the modeled financed outcome.

Issued shares of 2.5543 crore plus 0.1077 crore potential warrant shares give a conservative denominator of 2.662 crore shares. The base case excludes the unreceived ₹97.8993 crore exercise balance; the ₹1,212 exercise price exceeds the ₹763.30 dated quote. The conditional-receipt sensitivity includes the remaining cash and corresponding claims, without assuming exercise is certain. The existing 25% deposit is already in March cash and is not added again.

Credit-loss stresses reduce opening recoverable working capital, charge profit after tax, add back the noncash impairment and fund the required closing working-capital balance once. They are not separate immediate cash payments. No tax shield is assumed. Hypothetical losses of ₹25 crore and ₹50 crore are not forecasts of a joint-venture claim.

Exit operating-NOPAT multiples of 9, 12 and 16 times, and 7 times in the severe case, are analyst assumptions for cyclical manufacturing rather than imported peer multiples. The model assumes no dividend or immediate cash realization from associates. The final stub produces an exact five-year nominal INR return.
